title: R' Ivo (or Ayvo)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman says that he merited further to receive from all the great Amoraim of the first and second generations, as we find: R' Ivo said in the name of R' Yannai (Pesachim 46a, Ketubot 54b, Kiddushin 19a and 33a, Zevachim 103a). He also said in the name of R' Yochanan (Bereshit Rabbah ch. 82:5): R' Yudan and R' Ivo and R' Mashin bar Nagra in the name of R' Yochanan; and in Bereshit Rabbah ch. 12:6, Rav Huna (supplied ר״ה) in the name of Rabbi Yochanan, but Hyman says that there it should read, as the statement is brought at 11:2, “ר״ה” in the name of Rav, and R' Abahu in the name of R-Y.
In the name of R' Yosi ben Zimra, from Midrash Tehillim ch. 107:4.

In the name of Resh Lakish (Pesachim 46a). Those who say in his name: we find R' Yudan (Midrash Tehillim ch. 24:11), and there at ch. 8:20 R' Yehudah in his name, whom Hyman identifies without doubt as R' Yudan. R' Pinchas in his name in Bereshit Rabbah ch. 42:2.

Hyman also places him together with all the great preachers, such as with R' Yehudah bar R' Simon, as in Midrash Tehillim ch. 113:1, and with R' Shmuel bar Nachmani there ch. 94:3. And many of his homilies are found in the midrashim, and we will mention only his precious saying brought in Kohelet Rabbah 1:13 and 3:10: A person does not leave the world with half his desire in his hand; if he has a hundred, he wants to make them two hundred.

notes.text: Resh Lakish and Rabbi Yochanan are resolved from the connected context. The abbreviated RH remains a source question: the named Bereshit Rabbah11:3 is a bounded nonmatch, and12:6 has a longer Rav Huna–Rabbi Ayvu–Rabbi Yochanan chain. Hyman’s proposed emendation is retained without claiming these snippets prove its entire reconstruction.

The whole saved Midrash Rabbah -- TE Bereshit Rabbah12:6 scalar (5390 characters) was read and checked against its raw SHA256, selector and actual edition metadata. Its relevant chain is full Rav Huna REPORTS full Rabbi Ayvu REPORTS full Rabbi Yochanan. The vocalized digital form is אַיְּבוּ, not a replacement for supplied Ivo איבו or heading Ayvo אייבו. The first R-H can be expanded locally as Rav Huna, while Hyman's shorter Huna/Yochanan wording remains his supplied summary; the extra Ayvu reporting link and the fire-blessing teaching are described here, not inserted into the translated body. Full Rabbi before Yochanan is supported only in that local12:6 chain, not transferred to the earlier82:5 citation, the unlocated11:3 reconstruction, or the rest of the notice. The second R-H stays initialled, and R-Y in Hyman's proposed11:3 chain stays unexpanded; the historical Yochanan expansion remains exact in the old English. The old Hoshaya guess is archived, not adopted or converted into a new Huna identity. The previous chapter11/nonmatching11:3 checks remain bounded historical nonmatches, not global absence across editions or proof of a printed correction. No new whole11:3 witness was read. Hyman's definite THERE IT SHOULD READ remains expressly attributed with full force, not weakened to perhaps and not applied as an actual emendation. The explicit full Rav in the proposed chain stays Rav. Unsupported abbreviated titles in the heading, Ivo/Yannai,82:5 Yudan/Ivo/Mashin/Yochanan, Yose/Yosi, Yehudah/Yudan, Pinchas and the preacher list remain R'. The inherited Resh Lakish rendering of R-L is contextual and remains, not a fresh Pesachim passage binding. The source Yosi יוסי is distinguished from older Yose, with the latter archived; Ivo/Ayvo/Ayvu, Yudan/Yehudah, Mashin bar Nagra and all bar/ben forms are not harmonized or identity-bound. Yehudah bar R' Simon restores the father's abbreviated title explicitly supplied in the preacher list; it is not a title transfer from an unrelated Rabbi Yehudah bar Simon in the selected scalar. Hyman's merited STILL/FROM ALL/FIRST AND SECOND generations and WITH ALL great preachers remain attributed source claims rather than admitted chronology or associations. Every REPORTS/IN HIS NAME direction is retained; the abbreviated initial quoted saying is not turned into a new independent authority relationship. Hyman's Yehudah IS WITHOUT DOUBT Yudan identification retains its definite force but is expressly his claim, not an automatic merge. His ONLY THIS PRECIOUS SAYING, many homilies, and first-person WE FIND/WE WILL MENTION remain. The closing maxim keeps NOT LEAVE WORLD/HALF HIS DESIRE IN HIS HAND, conditional IF HE HAS ONE HUNDRED and WANTS TO MAKE THEM TWO HUNDRED, without importing a different maxim, an extra quantity or an economic assertion. All supplied locators retain chapter/section distinctions, including BR82section5/12section6/11section3, MidTehillim107section4/24section11/8section20/113section1/94section3 and BR42section2; Kohelet1section13 AND3section10 remain separate, and Kiddushin19a AND33a are not a range. No new whole witnesses for those other locations were read. Other figures, Adam/light/fire narratives, verses and legal continuations in the full5390char scalar are not imported. Both original mixed notes, the current mixed note, every old English version and every root intermediate remain exact; only this qualification is appended. p001 stays held with no canonical Hebrew repair, note retirement, publication or semantic/authority admission.

The whole printed notice is in volume I, p. 138. The whole consulted Bereshit Rabbah 12:6 has Rav Huna reporting Rabbi Ayvu reporting Rabbi Yochanan, including the intermediate Ayvu missing from Hyman’s abbreviated chain. The other chain is directly present in the whole 11:2 passage: Rav Huna in the name of Rav, and Rabbi Abbahu in the name of Rabbi Yochanan. The English cites this consulted 11:2 location beside Hyman’s supplied 11:3; the Hebrew and existing notes remain unchanged. The new comparison supersedes the earlier limited failure to locate that chain, without proving Hyman’s correction history or identifying every abbreviated name globally. His definite “there it should read” remains his argument. In the whole Pesachim 46a passage, the introductory name is Ayvu, but the quoted Hebrew attribution has Rabbi (Iniya) in the name of Rabbi Yannai, while Davidson’s English gives Rabbi Ayvu. These are disclosed readings, not silently harmonized persons. The extra four-mil and leather discussion is not inserted into Hyman’s biography. His claims about all the great teachers of two generations and all the great preachers, and his identification of Yehudah with Yudan “without doubt,” remain expressly his claims. The maxim keeps half one’s desire, one hundred and two hundred, without an added economic claim. The exact other cited passages and printings have not been newly collated here. All existing notes remain verbatim as records of their earlier review stages.
